solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Light sleeve unknown in khaki wearers? (4,4)

blocks.note: to light on something is to land on it, as a bird alights
the arm of a garment is its sleeve
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

annotation.surface: A light-coloured sleeve looks out of place among soldiers in khaki.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as pale, but it is the verb, to settle on. The Women's Land Army was the British wartime force of farm workers, uniformed in khaki-brown breeches; the question mark flags the loose definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Land Army's members wore a khaki-toned uniform, so they are, playfully, khaki wearers.

entries.clue: Red flag is flying round end of bayou as protection for swimmers (10)

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered
the anagrammed letters go round the U

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
last letter of BAYOU, set inside the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A red flag flies over a swamp on the bayou as a warning to bathers.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a real beach scene: a red flag means no swimming, and lifeguards fly it.
annotation.definitionFit: Lifeguards watch over swimmers and protect them from drowning.

entries.clue: Born in endless want (3)

indicators.note: the word loses its end letter

blocks.note: to want something is to lack it
the four-letter word loses its final D

annotation.surface: Someone born into never-ending poverty.
annotation.walkthrough: NÉE is French for born, used before a woman's maiden name: Mrs Smith, née Jones.
annotation.definitionFit: Née literally means born, as in 'née Jones'.

entries.clue: Missed kick, as one may observe on a blistering day? (3,4)

definitions.text: as one may observe on a blistering day?

blocks.note: a golf or football term for a swing that connects with nothing

blocks.clueFragment: as one may observe on a blistering day?
blocks.note: what you might remark about the atmosphere on a scorching day, split 3,1,3

annotation.surface: A footballer fluffs a kick in sweltering heat.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: split differently, AIR SHOT becomes 'air's hot', just what you would say on a blistering day. The question mark flags the wordplay-as-definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An air shot is a strike at a ball that misses it entirely.

entries.clue: Moving volume with Emma abroad — yes, primarily (6,6)

definitions.text: Moving volume with Emma abroad — yes, primarily

indicators.note: letters on the move are rearranged
take the first letter of 'yes'

blocks.note: v = volume
anagram fodder, 10 letters
first letter of YES

annotation.surface: A touching book in which Emma travels abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Flaubert's novel is a moving volume whose heroine is Emma Bovary, and in its French setting she is 'abroad' to an English reader.
annotation.definitionFit: Madame Bovary is Flaubert's novel of Emma Bovary, a moving book with Emma in France.

entries.clue: What transmits uniform string sound (6)

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a plink is the sound of a plucked string

annotation.surface: Asking what sends out the uniform tone of a string.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform string sound' reads as one phrase about an even note; 'uniform' is just its letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An uplink is the connection that transmits signals from the ground up to a satellite.

entries.clue: Forward matter involving FA official in March (7)

indicators.note: the outer word involves, or includes, the inner one

blocks.note: to march is to pace
a football (FA) official is a referee, REF

annotation.surface: A forward's case being handled by a Football Association official in March.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forward' and 'FA' conjure football; 'Forward matter' is front matter in a book, with a nod to foreword. The capital M hides the verb march.
annotation.definitionFit: A preface is material placed at the front of a book, before the main text.

entries.clue: I’m a jockey caught in situation and changing colours (11)

indicators.note: C goes in the word for situation

blocks.note: a jockey describing himself might say 'I ride'
situation = scene
c = caught, in cricket scoring; placed inside SCENE to make SCENCE

annotation.surface: A jockey reports being caught up in a scene and swapping racing silks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing colours' pulls toward jockeys' silks, but it describes a shimmer. 'I'm a jockey' is read as 'I ride'.
annotation.definitionFit: Iridescence is a play of colours that change with the angle of view, as on a soap bubble.

entries.clue: Like enthusiastic? That’s got it (4)

indicators.note: the preceding words have the answer inside them

blocks.note: liKE ENthusiastic

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a word means 'like enthusiastic' and is told they have got it.
annotation.walkthrough: Read straight, the whole clue is a gloss: something like 'enthusiastic', and those very words have it inside them.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue reads straight as an &lit: keen is a word like enthusiastic, and 'Like enthusiastic' contains it.

entries.clue: Unemployed remain unchanged, getting something for nothing (4,4)

blocks.note: unemployed = free, not engaged
to let something ride is to leave it unchanged

annotation.surface: Staying out of work and living off benefits.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a complaint about idlers. 'Ride' in the sense of 'let it ride' means to be left alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A free ride is a benefit enjoyed without paying for it.

entries.clue: Disguise the nature of surrounding Zulu country (6)

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: to belie is to give a false idea of
Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Disguising the character of the land around the Zulu people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Zulu country' looks like one phrase for KwaZulu or South Africa; Zulu is only its letter, and the country is in Central America.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the former British Honduras, on the Caribbean coast of Central America, is an independent nation.

entries.clue: Secretly represented colliery seat (12)

indicators.note: the letters are re-presented in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A mining constituency covertly represented in Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Represented colliery seat' reads as an MP for a coal-mining constituency.
annotation.definitionFit: Esoterically means in a way understood only by an inner circle, hence secretly.

entries.clue: Understand secure subjects given by guru (3,3,7)

blocks.note: to secure is to get
subjects = themes
a guru is a sage; 'given by' puts it next

annotation.surface: Grasping the topics a guru teaches.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces break across the answer's word boundaries, so 'subjects' cannot be read as the answer's last word; a guru is the classic crossword wise man.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: receiving and taking in a hint, the phrase is everyday English for grasping what someone means.

entries.clue: Who might improve avenues, getting green routes in order (4,7)

indicators.note: the letters are put into order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A town planner tidying up avenues and sorting out green routes.
annotation.walkthrough: Avenues are tree-lined streets, so the person who might improve them is the one who tends their trees.
annotation.definitionFit: A tree surgeon prunes and treats trees, which could improve a tree-lined avenue.

entries.clue: Light mood with papa hiding return of illness (6,4)

indicators.note: SPIRIT + P hides the reversed word
the word for illness is turned back

blocks.note: mood = spirit, as in high spirits
P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
mal = illness, as in petit mal and mal de mer; reversed to LAM and hidden before the P

annotation.surface: A cheerful mood while father keeps quiet about a relapse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return of illness' sounds like a relapse, but it means the word MAL written backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a small burner fuelled by methylated spirit gives off light, so 'Light' names the general kind.

entries.clue: Parry’s Requiem initially covered in a review (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of Requiem
R is wrapped inside the review

blocks.note: the letter a
to vet is to review
first letter of REQUIEM, placed inside VET to make VERT

annotation.surface: A critic's verdict on the Requiem by the composer Parry.
annotation.walkthrough: Hubert Parry was an English composer, so 'Parry's Requiem' reads as a musical work; here Parry is the verb and ’s means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A fencing sense: to parry a thrust is to turn it aside, which is what warding off a danger means.

entries.clue: British speak up about opening of chemical plant (9)

indicators.note: UTTER UP goes about the C
take the first letter of chemical

blocks.note: b = British
speak = utter
first letter of CHEMICAL
UP is used as it stands

annotation.surface: A British demand to speak up about the opening of a chemical works.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chemical plant' is a factory; 'plant' alone is the definition, a flower. 'Up' is used just as printed.
annotation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow-flowered plant.

entries.clue: Clean screen for protection of readers? (4,5)

blocks.note: to dust is to clean
to screen is to cover

annotation.surface: Wiping a screen protector for someone's reading glasses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Readers' suggests reading glasses or people; the question mark flags that the readers are books, which a dust jacket protects.
annotation.definitionFit: A dust cover is the paper jacket protecting a book, something read.

entries.clue: Fancy island church (7)

blocks.note: Capri, the island in the Bay of Naples
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: An elaborate church on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective describing the church; it is the noun, a whim.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: a fancy is a whim, a sudden impulsive notion.

entries.clue: Feasible idea when introducing nitrogen is one doomed to failure (5)

indicators.note: N is introduced into the word

blocks.note: a goer is an idea likely to work
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

annotation.surface: Adding nitrogen to a promising scheme dooms it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pits a feasible idea against one doomed to fail, and the two are one letter apart.
annotation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something past saving.

entries.clue: Site of old massacre showing delight welcoming new business (7)

indicators.note: the outer word welcomes the others inside

blocks.note: delight = glee
n = new
CO = company, a business

annotation.surface: A historic massacre site now thriving on new tourist trade.
annotation.walkthrough: Glencoe is a Scottish glen where the MacDonalds were massacred in 1692.
annotation.definitionFit: The Massacre of Glencoe took place there in 1692.

entries.clue: Charge for revolutionary soldiers before time for reconciliation (13)

blocks.note: a rap is a criminal charge
pro = for, in favour of
Che Guevara, the standard crossword revolutionary
soldiers = men
t = time, placed after MEN

annotation.surface: An accusation against rebel troops ahead of peace talks.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'for' is wordplay (PRO); the second is the link to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is the restoring of friendly relations, a reconciliation.

entries.clue: Nearly all reject incentive (4)

indicators.note: all but the last letter is kept

blocks.note: to reject with scorn
the five-letter word loses its final N

annotation.surface: Turning down almost every bonus offered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' looks like a quantity of rejections; it trims the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the rider's spur pricks a horse onward, so anything goading a person into action is one.

entries.clue: Summary of betting odds with exchange of vocal elements (6)

indicators.note: an exchange is a trade, each side handing over what the other had, so the two vowels trade places

blocks.note: a bookmaker's odds are his prices, as in starting price
the vowels I and E in PRICES swap places

annotation.surface: A summary of the betting, with a change of voices from the commentators.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vocal elements' means vowels, the voiced letters; swap PRICES' I and E and you have PRECIS.
annotation.definitionFit: A précis is a short summary of a text.

entries.clue: Don helps to fill this freshly-made slab cake (5,3)

annotation.definitionFit: The River Don drains, via the Sea of Azov, into the Black Sea, helping to fill it.

entries.clue: Fire mostly in cavity (3)

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

SACK without its last letter K

annotation.surface: A fire burning mostly inside a hollow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fire' reads as flames; it is the verb, to dismiss.
annotation.definitionFit: A sac is a hollow pouch-like cavity in a plant or animal.

entries.clue: Mule, perhaps one in a horse race (6)

blocks.note: a drug mule carries contraband across borders for a smuggling gang
any horse taking part, as in 'ten ran'

annotation.surface: A mule, of all animals, entered in a horse race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mule' pulls toward the animal, which suits the horse race; it is the smuggler.

entries.clue: Jockey reported winning, bagging Cheltenham’s first trophy (5,3)

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we take the spoken sound of the jockey word
to bag something is to pocket it, so UP holds the C inside
take Cheltenham's first letter

blocks.note: a jockey is a rider
winning = up, ahead
first letter of CHELTENHAM, bagged by UP

annotation.surface: A jockey is said to be leading and to have landed the Cheltenham Gold Cup.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is the English racecourse, so the surface is all horse racing; the trophy is golf's, the Ryder Cup contested by Europe and the USA.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ryder Cup is the trophy of the biennial Europe v USA golf match.
